## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
# Logistic Regression 
 
library(readxl)
 
# Load and skip the first row using read_excel
credit_card_default <- read_excel("C:/Users/anjan/Downloads/default of credit card clients.xls",
                                   col_names = TRUE)
 
# Show the structure of the dataset
str(credit_card_default)
 
names(credit_card_default)
 
names(credit_card_default)[names(credit_card_default) == "default payment next month"] <- "Default"
 
# Check if the column names are changed
names(credit_card_default)
 
# Build a logistic regression model to predict default using PAY_0, BILL_AMT1 and LIMIT_BAL as predictors
logistic_model <- glm(Default ~ PAY_0 + BILL_AMT1 + LIMIT_BAL, data = credit_card_default, family = binomial)
summary(logistic_model)
 
# Calculate the r squared value and the adjusted r squared value
r_squared <- 1 - (logistic_model$deviance / logistic_model$null.deviance)
n_squared <- 1 - (1 - r_squared) * (nrow(credit_card_default) - 1) / (nrow(credit_card_default) - length(logistic_model$coefficients) - 1)
r_squared
n_squared
 
# Calculate a confusion matrix to evaluate the model
predicted_probabilities <- predict(logistic_model, type = "response")
predicted_classes <- ifelse(predicted_probabilities > 0.5, 1, 0)
confusion_matrix <- table(Predicted = predicted_classes, Actual = credit_card_default$Default)
confusion_matrix
 
accuracy <- sum(diag(confusion_matrix)) / sum(confusion_matrix)
accuracy
 
# Add an interaction term between BILL_AMT1 and LIMIT_BAL and build a new model using the
# interaction term, sex, age, and education as predictors
new_logistic_model <- glm(
  Default ~ PAY_0 + BILL_AMT1 * LIMIT_BAL + SEX + AGE + EDUCATION,
  data = credit_card_default,
  family = binomial
)
summary(new_logistic_model)
 
# Calculate the r squared value and the adjusted r squared value for the new model
r_squared_new <- 1 - (new_logistic_model$deviance / new_logistic_model$null.deviance)
n_squared_new <- 1 - (1 - r_squared_new) * (nrow(credit_card_default) - 1) / (nrow(credit_card_default) - length(new_logistic_model$coefficients) - 1)
r_squared_new
n_squared_new
 
# Calculate a confusion matrix to evaluate the new model
predicted_probabilities_new <- predict(new_logistic_model, type = "response")
predicted_classes_new <- ifelse(predicted_probabilities_new > 0.5, 1, 0)
confusion_matrix_new <- table(Predicted = predicted_classes_new, Actual = credit_card_default$Default)
confusion_matrix_new
 
accuracy_new <- sum(diag(confusion_matrix_new)) / sum(confusion_matrix_new)
accuracy_new
 
# Calculate AIC to compare the two models
aic_original <- AIC(logistic_model)
aic_new <- AIC(new_logistic_model)
aic_original
aic_new
```
